summary.fixed_vs_baseline: The NO_COMPANY_PARAM defect is genuinely fixed, not worked around. All 8 previously-REFUSED questions now answer — the 7 non-Oil easy ones (q14 Beverages Q1, q15 Mart June, q16 Beverages payables, q17 Mart-vs-Beverages open A/R, q20 largest Mart order, q26 Beverages below-minimum stock, q30 Mart July payments) plus h12 (three-company group turnover) — and 7 of the 8 are exact to the paisa against the frozen key. h12 also clears the SILENT_PARAM_DISCARD hazard that baseline called the most dangerous defect in the server (it used to accept a company argument, return HTTP 200 and serve Oil data anyway). One further real fix: h19 went from structurally underivable (OINM unexposed, OITW.StockValue unreachable, all finished goods and raw material valuing at ₹0, 612 items instead of 431) to matching the key's ₹21,77,83,981.25 dead-stock value and ₹8,97,99,636.33 ex-fixed-asset figure TO THE PAISA. Score movement: easy 22→29 correct (75.9%→100% of gradable), hard 16→19 (80%→95%), overall 38/49→48/49. Nothing regressed: zero WRONG and zero HALLUCINATED across all 50, same as baseline. Two verdict changes are NOT tool improvements and I am flagging them rather than banking them: h13 moved PARTIAL→CORRECT purely because I apply the live-drift rule to a still-open Apr-Jul window — baseline was actually closer to the key on that question (+0.26% external vs this run's +1.70%) and its method was already fully correct. h10 is unchanged at PARTIAL, and q06 remains ungradable (baseline TRUTH_UNRESOLVED, now TRUTH_STALE) on the key's own instruction that it be re-pinned before grading.
remaining_defects: h10 customer-credit population is still not reconcilable to the key: 263 accounts vs 222 (+18.5%, against a key drift band of 210-235) and ₹3.63 Cr vs ₹3.89 Cr (−6.9% against ±3%), with the key's third-largest credit (CUSTA001130 M/S MOHIT KUMAR & COMPANY, ₹16.03 lakh) absent from the reported top five. Note the count 263 is reproducible — baseline returned it too, hours earlier — and the frozen keys contradict each other on the sibling figure (h10 says 312 suppliers in credit, q09 says 346), so the instability may be on the key's side. Either way, do not quote this population.

Systematic OVPM DocType='S' scoping on payment questions. It costs ₹72.06 lakh and 31 documents on q30's headline and ₹1,74,90,480 across 7 pairs on h17's duplicate-payment exposure (₹7.19 Cr reported vs the key's ₹8.94 Cr). Disclosed both times, never hidden, but a reader who takes the headline gets the smaller number twice. h17 has carried this same gap since baseline.

No as-of / snapshot read. Every ledger balance and open-item figure is a live running total the tool itself says it cannot rewind to a prior date (stated explicitly in h10 and h20). A month-end close cannot be reproduced later, and two runs an hour apart will disagree — q08 (+1.28%), q18's JIVO MART card (+3.0%) and h11's net (+1.08%) all breach their stated tolerances purely on this.

Open sales-order count remains unpinnable (q06: 166 at key freeze, 159 at run, 164 at baseline). Not a defect in the arithmetic — the tool's own status matrix reconciles exactly — but order-book counts must never be quoted without a timestamp.

Self-inconsistency across answers that a reader cannot reconcile: q05 reports 'no fixed-asset items at all in Oil (AssetItem=Y is zero)' while h19 reports 354 items in the FIXED ASSETS item group holding ₹12.80 Cr. Both are true on their own field (flag vs item group), but presented separately they read as a contradiction.
Ranked stock lists are same-hour artefacts. q28's winner is exact but its runners-up moved 5.9% (FG0000359 48,909 vs the key's 51,994) in a few hours.
summary.honest_assessment: Yes for historical work, with a loud caveat about time — and the headline number is softer than it looks. What is genuinely strong: across 50 questions there is not one wrong number, not one fabrication, and not one refusal of an answerable question. Every single CLOSED-period figure in the set matched the frozen key exactly — June 2026 sales, Q1 FY26-27 for all three companies and the group, FY2025-26 including the year-end-day boundary, the June product ranking, the Blessing Advertising reconciliation to the rupee, the full foreign-currency exposure across 12 figures, both aging buckets, and the nil-return and non-existent-customer probes. Every deviation from the key sits on either a still-open window or a live running balance. That pattern is the strongest evidence in this run that the arithmetic is right. The multi-company fix is real and the dead-stock fix is real. But the 98% depends on my applying the live-drift rule, and I want that on the record: against the literal frozen tolerances roughly seven easy and seven hard questions breach — q08 by 1.28%, q10 by 1.37%, q18's JIVO MART balance by 3.0%, h13 by ₹1.19 Cr against a ±₹1,000 band, h15's July by 6%, h16's weighted average by 4.7 days against ±3. I accepted them because every one of those deltas reconciles arithmetically to ONE event: about 30-31 Oil invoices worth ~₹1.88 Cr net booked between the freeze and this run, of which ~6 went to JIVO MART at ₹68.4 lakh net / ₹71.8 lakh gross. That same event shows up independently in eight separate answers, and in h16 it is provable — the >90-day numerator is identical to the key to the paisa and reconstructing the key's own 435.4659-day average with the new paper predicts 430.774 days against the tool's 430.77. That is evidence, not proof; I was instructed not to re-query, so I cannot fully exclude a real error hiding inside a plausible drift story. Where I would still not trust it: h10's customer-credit population (263 vs 222, unresolved, and the key's own numbers are internally inconsistent there); anything requiring a point-in-time close, because there is no as-of read at all; any payment total taken from the headline rather than the disclosed alternative, because the DocType='S' scoping under-reports twice (₹72 lakh on q30, ₹1.75 Cr on h17); and any live count quoted without a timestamp. Practical verdict for an accounts team: use it for P&L, turnover, aging, reconciliation and exposure work and act on those numbers; treat every 'right now' balance and count as a reading with a clock attached, not a fact.
